title: Write the call that starts the threads
starter:
let call_site (id : int) (n : int) (fields : string list) : string =
  ""
hints: Build the line from three pieces: the struct being filled, the call, and the closing brace.
`String.concat ", " fields` joins the field values with a comma and a space.
`Printf.sprintf "{ thread%d_ctx k_ = { %s }; uir_parallel_for(%d, thread%d, &k_); }" id (String.concat ", " fields) n id` is the whole line.
explain: The line does two things. It fills a fresh context struct with the current values of the body's free variables, in the same order as the struct's fields. Then it hands `uir_parallel_for` the trip count, the outlined function and the struct's address. The number `id` appears twice, in the struct's type and in the function's name, so a kernel with two thread loops gets two separate pairs.

tests.expect: { thread0_ctx k_ = { b0, r3 }; uir_parallel_for(64, thread0, &k_); }
{ thread0_ctx k_ = { b0, b2, r8, v7, v9 }; uir_parallel_for(64, thread0, &k_); }
{ thread1_ctx k_ = { b0, b1, b2 }; uir_parallel_for(192, thread1, &k_); }
{ thread2_ctx k_ = { b0, b1 }; uir_parallel_for(4, thread2, &k_); }
